breaks.quote: And it doesn’t start from zero. Somewhere in your life, you have already changed something without noticing.
breaks.why: The closing lines drop in new ideas with no example, reason or step, so the reader is left holding claims they cannot use.

breaks.quote: Lasting Change works with the part of you that wants to stay the same, one step at a time, in an order it can accept.
breaks.why: The method is named and asserted with no example or explanation of what working with that part looks like.

breaks.quote: Because it is not finished with you. It still has a lesson to teach, and you have not learned it yet.
breaks.why: The surprising claim that old regret holds a lesson comes with no example or reason, and the chimp story does not show it.

breaks.quote: tell it as a story about somebody else and find the moral. That is why there is a chimpanzee in my notes.
breaks.why: A new technique is dropped in as one sentence with no steps, and the link from chimps to the reader's regret is a leap the reader must guess.
The jump from years of sending an assistant to confidence is given no steps, so the reader has to guess how it happened.
